verdict.rationale:
Ubuntu is documented as freely installable on a huge range of third-party hardware (Dell, HP, Lenovo, Raspberry Pi, older machines, dual-boot or replace Windows) with no proprietary lock-in, and includes docs for driver installation (NVIDIA), disk encryption, and hardware certification. Community threads confirm real-world usage across diverse hardware, though some note friction with proprietary GPU drivers on certain machines, a minor practical caveat rather than a contradiction of the no-lock-in claim.
missing for 10: independent benchmarking across a wide hardware matrix, and explicit vendor commentary confirming freedom from lock-in beyond marketing copy.
